objective_for_doctor: A 42-year-old F patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: fever.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
I have a fever and a cough. I also have greenish or yellowish nasal discharge and pain around both eyes (right and left) that radiates to the back of my head and the temples on both sides.

Doctor: When did your symptoms start, and have you had any facial/forehead pressure that worsens when you bend forward?  
Doctor: Do you have any shortness of breath, chest pain, or severe sore throat, and have you measured your highest temperature?

I don’t know.  

Also, I have had pneumonia, polyps in my nose, and a deviated nasal septum. I have a cough and fever, and I have greenish or yellowish nasal discharge.

Doctor: Given your nasal polyps and green/yellow discharge, do you have worsening facial pressure or pain when leaning forward, and is there any reduced sense of smell?  
Doctor: Also, have you noticed any ear pain or tooth pain, and do you have any severe headache/neck stiffness or vision changes?
Yes, I have reduced sense of smell.

Doctor: Thank you—reduced smell plus green/yellow discharge and bilateral eye-area pain suggests acute bacterial sinusitis. Do you have worsening facial pressure/pain when you bend forward, and are you having any severe headache or vision changes?  
Doctor: To confirm and rule out complications, REQUEST TEST: Sinus CT (or CT sinuses without contrast) and REQUEST TEST: CBC (with differential) .

Doctor: I need to narrow this down—on a 0–10 scale, how bad is your facial/eye-area pain or pressure, and does it get noticeably worse when you bend forward?  
Doctor: Also, do you have any vision changes (double vision, decreased vision, pain with eye movement) or severe headache/neck stiffness?

It’s 6 out of 10 for the pain intensity, and the pain appears at a pace of 5 out of 10. I don’t know about whether it gets worse when I bend forward. I don’t know about any vision changes or severe headache/neck stiffness.

Doctor: Thanks—sinusitis seems likely, but we need to assess danger signs: do you have any eye swelling around the eyelids, double vision, or pain with moving your eyes? Also, do you have severe headache that’s unlike your usual or neck stiffness?  
Doctor: If you can, do you have your CT/CBC results yet (REQUEST TEST: CT sinuses without contrast, REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential) so I can decide if this is uncomplicated acute bacterial rhinosinusitis versus a complication?

I don’t know about eye swelling around the eyelids, double vision, or pain with moving my eyes. I also don’t know about any severe headache that’s unlike my usual or any neck stiffness. I don’t have my CT/CBC results yet.

Doctor: Given fever + green/yellow nasal discharge + reduced smell and bilateral eye-area/facial pain, I’m leaning to **acute bacterial rhinosinusitis**; to ensure we’re not missing an orbital/intracranial complication, can you check one more thing: any eyelid/around-eye swelling or redness, trouble moving the eyes, or decreased vision?  
Doctor: Also, what’s your maximum measured temperature (or “no thermometer”), and how long has the illness been going on in days?

I don’t know about any eyelid/around-eye swelling or redness, trouble moving my eyes, or decreased vision.

I also don’t know my maximum measured temperature, or how long the illness has been going on in days.

Doctor: Since you have fever, green/yellow nasal discharge, bilateral eye/facial pain, and reduced sense of smell—with no known vision/eye-movement red flags—I suspect **acute bacterial rhinosinusitis** rather than a complication.  
Doctor: I need treatment today, but first: how many days has this been going on (roughly), and do you have tooth pain in the upper teeth or worsening facial pain with bending forward?  
Doctor: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute bacterial rhinosinusitis (likely acute bacterial rhinosinusitis with fever; evaluate for complications if vision changes/eye swelling or severe worsening headache develop).
